content_html:
For the last 20 years, I’ve been what many would call an obsessive video game collector. Nearly every weekend, I could be found at the crack of dawn at garage sales, flea markets, thrift stores, and estate sales searching for Nintendo treasures to add to my collection.

Over the decades, those early mornings have led to some incredible finds. I’ve rescued a broken Pokémon Snap Station and restored it to working condition. I’ve uncovered countless rare NES, SNES, and Nintendo 64 games, along with promotional displays, store signage, and other pieces of Nintendo history that most collectors never get the chance to see.

This story also involves finding a new treasure, but something way outside of what I ever expected to discover. So strap in, get yourself a snack or a cup of coffee, and let’s talk about how I found 97 never-before-seen variants of one of the most popular games in history.

The Discovery

The story starts in a small downtown retro store called OneStopWonders. The owner, Kevin Braun, is somebody who I’ve known for quite some time. He’s owned retro shops in a variety of sizes over the years, and I’ve purchased more items than I can count from his stores over that time.

Kevin started becoming interested in pinball machines, a hobby that I coincidentally shared, and one of his machines broke down. He asked me if I’d be willing to come take a look, and I was thrilled to do so. After about a day or two of tinkering, we got it back up and running. As we shared a moment of excitement seeing the game spring back to life, we started talking a bit about his shop and his plans for the future.

Kevin knew that I ran a website, and selling things online was something he really wanted to start doing. So an agreement was struck, and Kevin and I started working together selling some of the retro games from his store online. For me, it was an absolute thrill. There’s nothing in life I like more than sifting through old retro video games.

OneStopWonders in Waukesha, WI

Some time later, while we were discussing what items to list next, Kevin started telling me stories about some of the strange items that had made their way into his shop over the years. One of those stories involved a man whose grandfather owned a precious metal recovery service back in the late ’80s and early ’90s.

The story I was told was that he had a contract with many vendors to extract gold from circuit boards if a vendor wanted to get rid of old inventory. One of those vendors happened to be Nintendo.

According to Kevin, the box was jam-packed with NES games. The story goes on to reveal that the box of games was supposed to be melted down and salvaged for the gold on the contacts of the pins. But for whatever reason, this box never made it to salvage. Instead, it sat in a garage for over 20 years before finding its way into Kevin’s shop.

Kevin confessed that he had no idea of the value of what was in the box and simply saw an opportunity to sell each game for roughly $10 to $15 apiece. He purchased the box, put it in his storage unit, and there it sat untouched for several years. The truth is, Kevin completely forgot about the purchase. If you look at some of the other things he’s bought over the years, though, that wasn’t an uncommon occurrence.

After Kevin finished his story, I immediately could tell that the blood had drained from my face.

“Can I see the box? Do you still have it?”

Kevin responded, “Yeah, follow me!”

The games had been a few hundred feet away from me all this time.

A short walk to his storage unit, and tucked underneath boxes of old Halloween decorations, it sat, untouched for years.

The first sticker that I saw on the front of the box was in Japanese, but in English the letters “NES” were clearly spelled out. At this point, I had no idea what games would be in this box. So I pulled it out, hands shaking, and opened it up for the very first time.

Nothing could quite prepare me for what I saw inside the first time I opened it up. Rather than explain it to you, I think it’s better that I show you.

This is what I saw when I opened this box.

My heart stopped when I first saw this.

Inside, were 97 individually wrapped, brand-new copies of Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt. Each game was wrapped in the same baggie that would have come in an official NES console bundle. Tucked behind each cartridge was a brand-new, absolutely pristine manual for the game as well.

Seeing brand-new Nintendo games is an incredibly exciting thing for a game collector. But seeing 97 of them all lined up, all of them pristine, nearly knocked me straight on my ass.

But at the end of the day, this was Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt, one of the most common games ever produced. And while these were uncirculated, brand-new copies, I wasn’t quite sure what kind of value we were really looking at.

Kevin confessed to me that he had thought about this box recently and was getting ready to take it out of storage and sell each game for $14.99 apiece.

We sat there for some time deciding what we should do with this box, and eventually we both agreed that I would take the box with me, and do some research.

So I covered the box in plastic, walked in the rain back to my car, and took it home.

That’s where this story takes yet another unexpected turn.

The Box

The first thing that I noticed when I saw the box in storage was the Japanese sticker. But beyond that, two additional stickers were there. Next to the Japanese text was a sticker that read “NOA” and had a P.O. Box for where it was sent. On the other side was an inventory sticker with a product number, description, the quantity of cartridges in the box, and the date that this box was sent out.

The description read “Mario – Hunt Remanufactured NES.” The quantity read 100, which means three games had escaped the box at some point over the past 30 years. The date read 12/19/95, very late in the NES lifespan.

As a guy who just loves Nintendo history, I was more in love with the box than I was with its contents at the time. It’s rare to see factory shipping boxes of old Nintendo games, let alone one that originated from Japan, was sent to Nintendo of America, and finally was sent off to a recovery center in the Middle of Nowhere, Wisconsin.

Finally, I decided to find out what the Japanese label said. After running it through a translation app, I found that it read, “NES cassettes, assembled product, 100 pieces.”

Nothing earth-shattering, but at least good confirmation that this was the original box these games came in.

With that, I snapped some photos and uploaded them, along with a post describing what I had found, to a high-end gaming Facebook group that I am a part of. I asked if anybody had seen anything like this before, and judging by the responses, no one ever had.

That’s when the messages started to come in.

The Realization

As quickly as I put the post up, the direct messages started pouring into my inbox. Some collectors asked to buy all of them. Some people said what I had was clearly counterfeit.

But two messages stood out even more.

Around 15 minutes after the post had gone live, I received messages from two separate directors at two separate grading companies. Both of them almost immediately told me the same thing.

Something was strange about these cartridges.

Something about the images that I had sent set off a red flag in both of their minds. I was immediately asked for more photos of the cartridge and the manual, and I was even asked to take one of the cartridges apart so the board could be inspected.

Luckily, I’m the kind of nerd who has security-bit screwdrivers sitting on my desk for just this occasion.

So I got to work and took one of the cartridges apart.

After snapping all of the photos they had requested, I received the call I never expected. What I had found wasn’t just a box of pristine Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt cartridges. It was an undocumented, never before seen variant.

The back label was unlike anything that had been documented before. Instead of the standard English-only text, it featured multiple languages. The manufacturing codes on both the cartridge and instruction manual also differed, indicating these games were produced in late 1993. Even the manual contained previously undocumented text. Known manuals include the phrase “maintenance or repairs,” while this newly discovered version instead reads “maintenance or service.”

Special thanks to Joseph Leo for his help identifying and documenting the differences found in these cartridges and manuals.

“or repairs” on known manual vs “or service” on our manual.

Perhaps most puzzling of all, the manufacturing dates on both the cartridge and manual come after every known Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt bundle these games could have belonged to.

The date code 9340 translates to the 40th week of 1993, which corresponds to late August.

What we had found was the very last production run, and an undiscovered variant of Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt. Arguably one of the most beloved, and one of the most documented games in Nintendo history.

Not only that, but nearly every cartridge was pristine.

But that raised an even bigger question: Why were these created in the first place? Why would Nintendo manufacture new pack-in games in late 1993 for a console bundle that was no longer being sold?

Our best theory is that these cartridges were produced either as replacement stock for warranty repairs and refurbished systems or for a bundle that was planned but never released. The truth is, though, nobody knows for certain. For now, the exact reason these cartridges were manufactured is just one more mystery surrounding this incredible discovery.

The Plan

After some back and forth with Kevin, we decided to send the games to one of the grading companies that reached out: PSA. They wanted to inspect them, authenticate them, and find out exactly what these things were.

After a brief conversation with one of their directors, it was decided that instead of mailing these 97 cartridges to them, I would hand-deliver them the next day.

So, I packed all 97 cartridges into my carry-on luggage and boarded a 5 a.m. flight from Milwaukee, Wisconsin, to Orange County, California. There aren’t many things that will make a grown man sweat quite like walking through a TSA checkpoint with 97 little circuit boards in his bag. I was convinced I was going to get pulled aside for questioning, but apparently they’ve seen far stranger things. To my surprise, I made it through security without so much as a second glance.

Just a normal guy with 97 NES games in his carry on.

After arriving in California, I was picked up at the airport and taken to PSA’s headquarters. I’ve had quite a few things graded by PSA in the past, so it was pretty fun to see just how huge their campus was.

When I arrived, I unpacked the games and briefly chatted with one of the directors before I left. From what they could see, there was very little doubt that these games were real. Of course, the grading process would 100% confirm that, but at face value, this looked like the real deal.

I was also told that the games were in remarkably good condition, some of the best they had ever seen.

So I left them there. I was told the process could take several weeks and that they would let me know as soon as they had an idea of what they were working with.

And just like that, the cartridges were gone from my possession, and I headed home.

One of the nice things about PSA is that they give you the ability to see the status of your grading (for video games, at least) right on their website.

So over the next few days, I compulsively refreshed the page to see if any of them had been graded and whether it was possible that at least one of these would receive the world’s first PSA 10 for an NES cartridge.

Luckily, I would not have to wait very long. About a week later, the first grades started coming in.

And there it was.

12 games in total had been graded, with a little over half of them receiving the incredibly high score of 9.8, several grading a nearly as impressive 9.6, and one receiving the coveted, never-before-seen-on-an-NES-cartridge PSA 10.

A world’s first.

As the days went on, more cartridges completed the grading process. When all was said and done, a total of five PSA 10 cartridges were graded.

Shortly after, the boxes started arriving back home. 12 cartridges at a time were sent back to us, and I watched every tracking number like a hawk, ensuring nothing looked off during transportation.

Now What?

So what’s next?

What do you do with a collection like this?

Well, that’s the million-dollar question.

Kevin and I will be keeping an undecided number for ourselves. Some of the others will be auctioned off, and others will have charity auctions set up in the very near future.

Jason (Left) and Kevin (Right) looking at the PSA 10s for the first time

I’m happy to report that the first three games will be auctioned on August 12th at Goldin Auctions, including one of the PSA 10s. We will have more information about this auction in the immediate future. I’m also thrilled to say that full scans of the instruction manual, along with photos of every angle of the cartridge, will be available online in the coming days.

So that’s the story as of right now.

As a lifelong game collector, I don’t think I could have dreamed of a more exciting story. A box that was originally meant to be destroyed, and cartridges meant to be scrapped for the gold in their pins, somehow made its way from Japan to Seattle, Washington, to a smelting factory, and finally landed in a small retro shop in a small city in southeastern Wisconsin.

Sometimes the truth is a lot more exciting than fiction.

Stay tuned!

There’s nothing in life I like more than sifting through old retro video games.

sentences.en: Kevin knew that I ran a website, and selling things online was something he really wanted to start doing.
sentences.zh: 凯文知道我经营一个网站，而在线销售商品是他真正想开始做的事情。

sentences.en: So an agreement was struck, and Kevin and I started working together selling some of the retro games from his store online.
sentences.zh: 于是达成了一项协议，凯文和我开始合作从他的在线商店销售一些复古游戏。

sentences.en: For me, it was an absolute thrill.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这绝对是一种兴奋。

sentences.en: There’s nothing in life I like more than sifting through old retro video games.

blocks.html_en: OneStopWonders in Waukesha, WI

sentences.en: OneStopWonders in Waukesha, WI
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州沃克夏的一站式奇迹

blocks.html_en: Some time later, while we were discussing what items to list next, Kevin started telling me stories about some of the strange items that had made their way into his shop over the years. One of those stories involved a man whose grandfather owned a precious metal recovery service back in the late ’80s and early ’90s.

sentences.en: Some time later, while we were discussing what items to list next, Kevin started telling me stories about some of the strange items that had made their way into his shop over the years.
sentences.zh: 一段时间后，当我们讨论接下来要列出哪些商品时，凯文开始向我讲述多年来进入他店里的一些奇怪商品的故事。

sentences.en: One of those stories involved a man whose grandfather owned a precious metal recovery service back in the late ’80s and early ’90s.
sentences.zh: 其中一个故事涉及一名男子，他的祖父在 80 年代末和 90 年代初拥有一家贵金属回收服务公司。

blocks.html_en: The story I was told was that he had a contract with many vendors to extract gold from circuit boards if a vendor wanted to get rid of old inventory. One of those vendors happened to be Nintendo.

sentences.en: The story I was told was that he had a contract with many vendors to extract gold from circuit boards if a vendor wanted to get rid of old inventory.
sentences.zh: 我听说的故事是，他与许多供应商签订了合同，如果供应商想要摆脱旧库存，他可以从电路板上提取黄金。

sentences.en: One of those vendors happened to be Nintendo.
sentences.zh: 这些供应商之一恰好是任天堂。

blocks.html_en: According to Kevin, the box was jam-packed with NES games. The story goes on to reveal that the box of games was supposed to be melted down and salvaged for the gold on the contacts of the pins. But for whatever reason, this box never made it to salvage. Instead, it sat in a garage for over 20 years before finding its way into Kevin’s shop.

sentences.en: According to Kevin, the box was jam-packed with NES games.
sentences.zh: 据凯文说，盒子里塞满了红白机游戏。

sentences.en: The story goes on to reveal that the box of games was supposed to be melted down and salvaged for the gold on the contacts of the pins.
sentences.zh: 故事继续透露，游戏盒应该被熔化并打捞出来，以获取插针触点上的黄金。

sentences.en: But for whatever reason, this box never made it to salvage.
sentences.zh: 但无论出于什么原因，这个盒子一直没有被打捞上来。

sentences.en: Instead, it sat in a garage for over 20 years before finding its way into Kevin’s shop.
sentences.zh: 相反，它在车库里存放了 20 多年，然后才进入凯文的商店。

blocks.html_en: Kevin confessed that he had no idea of the value of what was in the box and simply saw an opportunity to sell each game for roughly $10 to $15 apiece. He purchased the box, put it in his storage unit, and there it sat untouched for several years. The truth is, Kevin completely forgot about the purchase. If you look at some of the other things he’s bought over the years, though, that wasn’t an uncommon occurrence.

sentences.en: Kevin confessed that he had no idea of the value of what was in the box and simply saw an opportunity to sell each game for roughly $10 to $15 apiece.
sentences.zh: 凯文承认，他不知道盒子里的东西的价值，只是看到了以每款大约 10 至 15 美元的价格出售每款游戏的机会。

sentences.en: He purchased the box, put it in his storage unit, and there it sat untouched for several years.
sentences.zh: 他买下了这个盒子，把它放在自己的储藏室里，几年来都没有动过。

sentences.en: The truth is, Kevin completely forgot about the purchase.
sentences.zh: 事实是，凯文完全忘记了购买的事。

sentences.en: If you look at some of the other things he’s bought over the years, though, that wasn’t an uncommon occurrence.
sentences.zh: 不过，如果你看看他这些年来买的其他一些东西，就会发现这种情况并不少见。

blocks.html_en: After Kevin finished his story, I immediately could tell that the blood had drained from my face.

sentences.en: After Kevin finished his story, I immediately could tell that the blood had drained from my face.
sentences.zh: 凯文讲完他的故事后，我立刻就看出我脸上的血色已经消失了。

blocks.html_en: “Can I see the box? Do you still have it?”

sentences.en: “Can I see the box?
sentences.zh: “我可以看一下盒子吗？

sentences.en: Do you still have it?”
sentences.zh: 你还有吗？

blocks.html_en: Kevin responded, “Yeah, follow me!”

sentences.en: Kevin responded, “Yeah, follow me!”
sentences.zh: 凯文回应道：“好，跟我来！”

blocks.html_en: The games had been a few hundred feet away from me all this time.

sentences.en: The games had been a few hundred feet away from me all this time.
sentences.zh: 比赛一直离我几百英尺远。

blocks.html_en: A short walk to his storage unit, and tucked underneath boxes of old Halloween decorations, it sat, untouched for years.

sentences.en: A short walk to his storage unit, and tucked underneath boxes of old Halloween decorations, it sat, untouched for years.
sentences.zh: 走一小段路就到了他的储藏室，里面藏着一盒旧的万圣节装饰品，多年来一直没有动过。

blocks.html_en: The first sticker that I saw on the front of the box was in Japanese, but in English the letters “NES” were clearly spelled out. At this point, I had no idea what games would be in this box. So I pulled it out, hands shaking, and opened it up for the very first time.

sentences.en: The first sticker that I saw on the front of the box was in Japanese, but in English the letters “NES” were clearly spelled out.
sentences.zh: 我在盒子正面看到的第一张贴纸是日文的，但英文字母“NES”却清楚地拼写出来。

sentences.en: At this point, I had no idea what games would be in this box.
sentences.zh: 此时，我不知道这个盒子里会装什么游戏。

sentences.en: So I pulled it out, hands shaking, and opened it up for the very first time.
sentences.zh: 于是我双手颤抖地把它拉出来，第一次打开它。

blocks.html_en: Nothing could quite prepare me for what I saw inside the first time I opened it up. Rather than explain it to you, I think it’s better that I show you.

sentences.en: Nothing could quite prepare me for what I saw inside the first time I opened it up.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次打开它时，没有什么能让我对里面看到的东西做好准备。

sentences.en: Rather than explain it to you, I think it’s better that I show you.
sentences.zh: 我认为与其向您解释，不如向您展示更好。

blocks.html_en: This is what I saw when I opened this box.

sentences.en: This is what I saw when I opened this box.
sentences.zh: 这是我打开这个盒子时看到的。

blocks.html_en: My heart stopped when I first saw this.

sentences.en: My heart stopped when I first saw this.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次看到这个时，我的心停止了跳动。

blocks.html_en: Inside, were 97 individually wrapped, brand-new copies of Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt. Each game was wrapped in the same baggie that would have come in an official NES console bundle. Tucked behind each cartridge was a brand-new, absolutely pristine manual for the game as well.

sentences.en: Inside, were 97 individually wrapped, brand-new copies of Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt.
sentences.zh: 里面有 97 份单独包装的全新《超级马里奥兄弟/猎鸭子》副本。

sentences.en: Each game was wrapped in the same baggie that would have come in an official NES console bundle.
sentences.zh: 每个游戏都装在与官方 NES 游戏机捆绑包相同的袋子中。

sentences.en: Tucked behind each cartridge was a brand-new, absolutely pristine manual for the game as well.
sentences.zh: 每个卡带后面都藏着一本全新的、绝对原始的游戏手册。

blocks.html_en: Seeing brand-new Nintendo games is an incredibly exciting thing for a game collector. But seeing 97 of them all lined up, all of them pristine, nearly knocked me straight on my ass.

sentences.en: Seeing brand-new Nintendo games is an incredibly exciting thing for a game collector.
sentences.zh: 对于游戏收藏家来说，看到全新的任天堂游戏是一件非常令人兴奋的事情。

sentences.en: But seeing 97 of them all lined up, all of them pristine, nearly knocked me straight on my ass.
sentences.zh: 但看到 97 个都排成一排，而且个个都是崭新的，我差点就惊呆了。

blocks.html_en: But at the end of the day, this was Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt, one of the most common games ever produced. And while these were uncirculated, brand-new copies, I wasn’t quite sure what kind of value we were really looking at.

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, this was Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt, one of the most common games ever produced.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，这就是《超级马里奥兄弟/猎鸭子》，有史以来最常见的游戏之一。

sentences.en: And while these were uncirculated, brand-new copies, I wasn’t quite sure what kind of value we were really looking at.
sentences.zh: 虽然这些是未流通的全新副本，但我不太确定我们真正关注的是哪种价值。

blocks.html_en: Kevin confessed to me that he had thought about this box recently and was getting ready to take it out of storage and sell each game for $14.99 apiece.

sentences.en: Kevin confessed to me that he had thought about this box recently and was getting ready to take it out of storage and sell each game for $14.99 apiece.
sentences.zh: 凯文向我坦白，他最近考虑过这个盒子，并准备将其从仓库中取出，并以每款 14.99 美元的价格出售每款游戏。

blocks.html_en: We sat there for some time deciding what we should do with this box, and eventually we both agreed that I would take the box with me, and do some research.

sentences.en: We sat there for some time deciding what we should do with this box, and eventually we both agreed that I would take the box with me, and do some research.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里坐了一段时间，决定我们应该如何处理这个盒子，最终我们都同意我会随身携带这个盒子，并做一些研究。

blocks.html_en: So I covered the box in plastic, walked in the rain back to my car, and took it home.

sentences.en: So I covered the box in plastic, walked in the rain back to my car, and took it home.
sentences.zh: 于是我用塑料盖住盒子，冒着雨走回车里，把它带回家。

blocks.html_en: That’s where this story takes yet another unexpected turn.

sentences.en: That’s where this story takes yet another unexpected turn.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个故事发生另一个意想不到的转折的地方。

blocks.html_en: The Box

sentences.en: The Box
sentences.zh: 盒子

blocks.html_en: The first thing that I noticed when I saw the box in storage was the Japanese sticker. But beyond that, two additional stickers were there. Next to the Japanese text was a sticker that read “NOA” and had a P.O. Box for where it was sent. On the other side was an inventory sticker with a product number, description, the quantity of cartridges in the box, and the date that this box was sent out.

sentences.en: The first thing that I noticed when I saw the box in storage was the Japanese sticker.
sentences.zh: 当我看到存放的盒子时，我首先注意到的是日本贴纸。

sentences.en: But beyond that, two additional stickers were there.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，还有另外两张贴纸。

sentences.en: Next to the Japanese text was a sticker that read “NOA” and had a P.O.
sentences.zh: 日文文字旁边有一张贴纸，上面写着“NOA”，并有一个 P.O.

sentences.en: Box for where it was sent.
sentences.zh: 发送地点的盒子。

sentences.en: On the other side was an inventory sticker with a product number, description, the quantity of cartridges in the box, and the date that this box was sent out.
sentences.zh: 另一面是一张库存标签，上面有产品编号、描述、盒子中墨盒的数量以及盒子的发出日期。

blocks.html_en: The description read “Mario – Hunt Remanufactured NES.” The quantity read 100, which means three games had escaped the box at some point over the past 30 years. The date read 12/19/95, very late in the NES lifespan.

sentences.en: The description read “Mario – Hunt Remanufactured NES.”
sentences.zh: 描述上写着“马里奥 – 亨特再造 NES”。

sentences.en: The quantity read 100, which means three games had escaped the box at some point over the past 30 years.
sentences.zh: 数量为 100，这意味着在过去 30 年的某个时刻，有三款游戏脱离了盒子。

sentences.en: The date read 12/19/95, very late in the NES lifespan.
sentences.zh: 日期显示为 12/19/95，在 NES 生命周期中已经很晚了。

blocks.html_en: As a guy who just loves Nintendo history, I was more in love with the box than I was with its contents at the time. It’s rare to see factory shipping boxes of old Nintendo games, let alone one that originated from Japan, was sent to Nintendo of America, and finally was sent off to a recovery center in the Middle of Nowhere, Wisconsin.

sentences.en: As a guy who just loves Nintendo history, I was more in love with the box than I was with its contents at the time.
sentences.zh: 作为一个热爱任天堂历史的人，我更喜欢这个盒子，而不是当时的里面的东西。

sentences.en: It’s rare to see factory shipping boxes of old Nintendo games, let alone one that originated from Japan, was sent to Nintendo of America, and finally was sent off to a recovery center in the Middle of Nowhere, Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 很少能看到工厂装运旧任天堂游戏的盒子，更不用说那些原产于日本、被送往美国任天堂、最后被送往威斯康星州偏远地区的回收中心的情况了。

blocks.html_en: Finally, I decided to find out what the Japanese label said. After running it through a translation app, I found that it read, “NES cassettes, assembled product, 100 pieces.”

sentences.en: Finally, I decided to find out what the Japanese label said.
sentences.zh: 最后我决定去看看日本厂牌是怎么说的。

sentences.en: After running it through a translation app, I found that it read, “NES cassettes, assembled product, 100 pieces.”
sentences.zh: 通过翻译应用程序运行后，我发现上面写着：“NES 卡带，组装品，100 件。”

blocks.html_en: Nothing earth-shattering, but at least good confirmation that this was the original box these games came in.

sentences.en: Nothing earth-shattering, but at least good confirmation that this was the original box these games came in.
sentences.zh: 没有什么惊天动地的事情，但至少很好地确认了这是这些游戏的原始盒子。

blocks.html_en: With that, I snapped some photos and uploaded them, along with a post describing what I had found, to a high-end gaming Facebook group that I am a part of. I asked if anybody had seen anything like this before, and judging by the responses, no one ever had.

sentences.en: With that, I snapped some photos and uploaded them, along with a post describing what I had found, to a high-end gaming Facebook group that I am a part of.
sentences.zh: 之后，我拍了一些照片，并将它们连同描述我所发现的内容的帖子一起上传到我所属的一个高端游戏 Facebook 群组。

sentences.en: I asked if anybody had seen anything like this before, and judging by the responses, no one ever had.
sentences.zh: 我问是否有人以前见过这样的事情，从回答来看，没有人见过。

blocks.html_en: That’s when the messages started to come in.

sentences.en: That’s when the messages started to come in.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，消息开始传入。

blocks.html_en: The Realization

sentences.en: The Realization
sentences.zh: 实现

blocks.html_en: As quickly as I put the post up, the direct messages started pouring into my inbox. Some collectors asked to buy all of them. Some people said what I had was clearly counterfeit.

sentences.en: As quickly as I put the post up, the direct messages started pouring into my inbox.
sentences.zh: 我一发布帖子，私信就开始涌入我的收件箱。

sentences.en: Some collectors asked to buy all of them.
sentences.zh: 一些收藏家要求全部购买。

sentences.en: Some people said what I had was clearly counterfeit.
sentences.zh: 有人说我的东西明显是假的。

blocks.html_en: But two messages stood out even more.

sentences.en: But two messages stood out even more.
sentences.zh: 但有两条信息更加引人注目。

blocks.html_en: Around 15 minutes after the post had gone live, I received messages from two separate directors at two separate grading companies. Both of them almost immediately told me the same thing.

sentences.en: Around 15 minutes after the post had gone live, I received messages from two separate directors at two separate grading companies.
sentences.zh: 帖子发布后大约 15 分钟，我收到了来自两家不同评级公司的两位董事的消息。

sentences.en: Both of them almost immediately told me the same thing.
sentences.zh: 他们俩几乎立刻就告诉了我同样的事情。

blocks.html_en: Something was strange about these cartridges.

sentences.en: Something was strange about these cartridges.
sentences.zh: 这些墨盒有些奇怪。

blocks.html_en: Something about the images that I had sent set off a red flag in both of their minds. I was immediately asked for more photos of the cartridge and the manual, and I was even asked to take one of the cartridges apart so the board could be inspected.

sentences.en: Something about the images that I had sent set off a red flag in both of their minds.
sentences.zh: 我发送的图片中的某些内容在他们俩的脑海中引发了危险信号。

sentences.en: I was immediately asked for more photos of the cartridge and the manual, and I was even asked to take one of the cartridges apart so the board could be inspected.
sentences.zh: 他们立即要求我提供更多墨盒和手册的照片，甚至要求我拆开其中一个墨盒，以便检查电路板。

blocks.html_en: Luckily, I’m the kind of nerd who has security-bit screwdrivers sitting on my desk for just this occasion.

sentences.en: Luckily, I’m the kind of nerd who has security-bit screwdrivers sitting on my desk for just this occasion.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我是那种书呆子，为了这个场合，我的桌子上放了安全螺丝刀。

blocks.html_en: So I got to work and took one of the cartridges apart.

sentences.en: So I got to work and took one of the cartridges apart.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始工作并拆开了其中一个墨盒。

blocks.html_en: After snapping all of the photos they had requested, I received the call I never expected. What I had found wasn’t just a box of pristine Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt cartridges. It was an undocumented, never before seen variant.

sentences.en: After snapping all of the photos they had requested, I received the call I never expected.
sentences.zh: 拍完他们要求的所有照片后，我接到了意想不到的电话。

sentences.en: What I had found wasn’t just a box of pristine Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt cartridges.
sentences.zh: 我发现的不仅仅是一盒原始的《超级马里奥兄弟/猎鸭》卡带。

sentences.en: It was an undocumented, never before seen variant.
sentences.zh: 这是一个未记录的、以前从未见过的变体。

blocks.html_en: The back label was unlike anything that had been documented before. Instead of the standard English-only text, it featured multiple languages. The manufacturing codes on both the cartridge and instruction manual also differed, indicating these games were produced in late 1993. Even the manual contained previously undocumented text. Known manuals include the phrase “maintenance or repairs,” while this newly discovered version instead reads “maintenance or service.”

sentences.en: The back label was unlike anything that had been documented before.
sentences.zh: 背面标签与之前记录的任何内容都不同。

sentences.en: Instead of the standard English-only text, it featured multiple languages.
sentences.zh: 它不是标准的纯英文文本，而是多种语言。

sentences.en: The manufacturing codes on both the cartridge and instruction manual also differed, indicating these games were produced in late 1993.
sentences.zh: 卡带和说明书上的制造代码也不同，表明这些游戏是 1993 年末生产的。

sentences.en: Even the manual contained previously undocumented text.
sentences.zh: 甚至该手册也包含以前未记录的文本。

sentences.en: Known manuals include the phrase “maintenance or repairs,” while this newly discovered version instead reads “maintenance or service.”
sentences.zh: 已知的手册包括“维护或维修”一词，而这个新发现的版本则改为“维护或维修”。

blocks.html_en: Special thanks to Joseph Leo for his help identifying and documenting the differences found in these cartridges and manuals.

sentences.en: Special thanks to Joseph Leo for his help identifying and documenting the differences found in these cartridges and manuals.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢 Joseph Leo 帮助识别和记录这些墨盒和手册中发现的差异。

blocks.html_en: “or repairs” on known manual vs “or service” on our manual.

sentences.en: “or repairs” on known manual vs “or service” on our manual.
sentences.zh: 已知手册中的“或维修”与我们手册中的“或服务”。

blocks.html_en: Perhaps most puzzling of all, the manufacturing dates on both the cartridge and manual come after every known Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt bundle these games could have belonged to.

sentences.en: Perhaps most puzzling of all, the manufacturing dates on both the cartridge and manual come after every known Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt bundle these games could have belonged to.
sentences.zh: 也许最令人费解的是，卡带和手册上的制造日期都晚于这些游戏可能所属的每个已知的《超级马里奥兄弟》/《猎鸭子》捆绑包。

blocks.html_en: The date code 9340 translates to the 40th week of 1993, which corresponds to late August.

sentences.en: The date code 9340 translates to the 40th week of 1993, which corresponds to late August.
sentences.zh: 日期代码 9340 翻译为 1993 年第 40 周，对应于 8 月下旬。

blocks.html_en: What we had found was the very last production run, and an undiscovered variant of Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt. Arguably one of the most beloved, and one of the most documented games in Nintendo history.

sentences.en: What we had found was the very last production run, and an undiscovered variant of Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的是最后一次生产运行，以及《超级马里奥兄弟/猎鸭子》的一个未被发现的变体。

sentences.en: Arguably one of the most beloved, and one of the most documented games in Nintendo history.
sentences.zh: 可以说是任天堂历史上最受欢迎、记录最多的游戏之一。

blocks.html_en: Not only that, but nearly every cartridge was pristine.

sentences.en: Not only that, but nearly every cartridge was pristine.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，几乎每个墨盒都是原始的。

blocks.html_en: But that raised an even bigger question: Why were these created in the first place? Why would Nintendo manufacture new pack-in games in late 1993 for a console bundle that was no longer being sold?

sentences.en: But that raised an even bigger question: Why were these created in the first place?
sentences.zh: 但这提出了一个更大的问题：为什么要创建这些？

sentences.en: Why would Nintendo manufacture new pack-in games in late 1993 for a console bundle that was no longer being sold?
sentences.zh: 为什么任天堂要在 1993 年底为不再销售的游戏机捆绑包制作新的游戏包？

content_html_zh:
在过去的 20 年里，我一直是许多人所说的痴迷的视频游戏收藏家。 几乎每个周末，黎明时分，我都会在车库拍卖、跳蚤市场、旧货店和房地产拍卖会上发现任天堂的宝藏，以添加到我的收藏中。

几十年来，那些清晨带来了一些令人难以置信的发现。 我救出了一个损坏的神奇宝贝快照站并将其恢复到工作状态。 我发现了无数稀有的 NES、SNES 和 Nintendo 64 游戏，以及促销展示、商店标牌和大多数收藏家从未有机会看到的其他任天堂历史作品。

这个故事还涉及寻找新的宝藏，但它超出了我的预期。 因此，请系好安全带，给自己准备一份零食或一杯咖啡，然后我们来谈谈我是如何发现历史上最受欢迎的游戏之一的 97 个前所未见的变体的。

发现号

故事始于市中心一家名为 OneStopWonders 的小型复古商店。 店主凯文·布劳恩（Kevin Braun）是我认识很久的人了。 多年来，他拥有各种规模的复古店，而我在那段时间从他的店里购买的商品多得数不过来。

凯文开始对弹球机产生兴趣，我碰巧也有同样的爱好，他的一台机器坏了。 他问我是否愿意过来看看，我很高兴这么做。 经过大约一两天的修补后，我们让它恢复正常并运行。 当我们分享了看到游戏重新焕发活力的兴奋时刻时，我们开始谈论他的商店和他对未来的计划。

凯文知道我经营一个网站，而在线销售商品是他真正想开始做的事情。 于是达成了一项协议，凯文和我开始合作从他的在线商店销售一些复古游戏。 对我来说，这绝对是一种兴奋。 生活中没有什么比筛选老式复古电子游戏更让我喜欢的了。

威斯康星州沃克夏的一站式奇迹

一段时间后，当我们讨论接下来要列出哪些商品时，凯文开始向我讲述多年来进入他店里的一些奇怪商品的故事。 其中一个故事涉及一名男子，他的祖父在 80 年代末和 90 年代初拥有一家贵金属回收服务公司。

我听说的故事是，他与许多供应商签订了合同，如果供应商想要摆脱旧库存，他可以从电路板上提取黄金。 这些供应商之一恰好是任天堂。

据凯文说，盒子里塞满了红白机游戏。 故事继续透露，游戏盒应该被熔化并打捞出来，以获取插针触点上的黄金。 但无论出于什么原因，这个盒子一直没有被打捞上来。 相反，它在车库里存放了 20 多年，然后才进入凯文的商店。

凯文承认，他不知道盒子里的东西的价值，只是看到了以每款大约 10 至 15 美元的价格出售每款游戏的机会。 他买下了这个盒子，把它放在自己的储藏室里，几年来都没有动过。 事实是，凯文完全忘记了购买的事。 不过，如果你看看他这些年来买的其他一些东西，就会发现这种情况并不少见。

凯文讲完他的故事后，我立刻就看出我脸上的血色已经消失了。

“我可以看一下盒子吗？ 你还有吗？

凯文回应道：“好，跟我来！”

比赛一直离我几百英尺远。

走一小段路就到了他的储藏室，里面藏着一盒旧的万圣节装饰品，多年来一直没有动过。

我在盒子正面看到的第一张贴纸是日文的，但英文字母“NES”却清楚地拼写出来。 此时，我不知道这个盒子里会装什么游戏。 于是我双手颤抖地把它拉出来，第一次打开它。

当我第一次打开它时，没有什么能让我对里面看到的东西做好准备。 我认为与其向您解释，不如向您展示更好。

这是我打开这个盒子时看到的。

当我第一次看到这个时，我的心停止了跳动。

里面有 97 份单独包装的全新《超级马里奥兄弟/猎鸭子》副本。 每个游戏都装在与官方 NES 游戏机捆绑包相同的袋子中。 每个卡带后面都藏着一本全新的、绝对原始的游戏手册。

对于游戏收藏家来说，看到全新的任天堂游戏是一件非常令人兴奋的事情。 但看到 97 个都排成一排，而且个个都是崭新的，我差点就惊呆了。

但归根结底，这就是《超级马里奥兄弟/猎鸭子》，有史以来最常见的游戏之一。 虽然这些是未流通的全新副本，但我不太确定我们真正关注的是哪种价值。

凯文向我坦白，他最近考虑过这个盒子，并准备将其从仓库中取出，并以每款 14.99 美元的价格出售每款游戏。

我们在那里坐了一段时间，决定我们应该如何处理这个盒子，最终我们都同意我会随身携带这个盒子，并做一些研究。

于是我用塑料盖住盒子，冒着雨走回车里，把它带回家。

这就是这个故事发生另一个意想不到的转折的地方。

盒子

当我看到存放的盒子时，我首先注意到的是日本贴纸。 但除此之外，还有另外两张贴纸。 日文文字旁边有一张贴纸，上面写着“NOA”，并有一个 P.O. 发送地点的盒子。 另一面是一张库存标签，上面有产品编号、描述、盒子中墨盒的数量以及盒子的发出日期。

描述上写着“马里奥 – 亨特再造 NES”。 数量为 100，这意味着在过去 30 年的某个时刻，有三款游戏脱离了盒子。 日期显示为 12/19/95，在 NES 生命周期中已经很晚了。

作为一个热爱任天堂历史的人，我更喜欢这个盒子，而不是当时的里面的东西。 很少能看到工厂装运旧任天堂游戏的盒子，更不用说那些原产于日本、被送往美国任天堂、最后被送往威斯康星州偏远地区的回收中心的情况了。

最后我决定去看看日本厂牌是怎么说的。 通过翻译应用程序运行后，我发现上面写着：“NES 卡带，组装品，100 件。”

没有什么惊天动地的事情，但至少很好地确认了这是这些游戏的原始盒子。

之后，我拍了一些照片，并将它们连同描述我所发现的内容的帖子一起上传到我所属的一个高端游戏 Facebook 群组。 我问是否有人以前见过这样的事情，从回答来看，没有人见过。

就在那时，消息开始传入。

实现

我一发布帖子，私信就开始涌入我的收件箱。 一些收藏家要求全部购买。 有人说我的东西明显是假的。

但有两条信息更加引人注目。

帖子发布后大约 15 分钟，我收到了来自两家不同评级公司的两位董事的消息。 他们俩几乎立刻就告诉了我同样的事情。

这些墨盒有些奇怪。

我发送的图片中的某些内容在他们俩的脑海中引发了危险信号。 他们立即要求我提供更多墨盒和手册的照片，甚至要求我拆开其中一个墨盒，以便检查电路板。

幸运的是，我是那种书呆子，为了这个场合，我的桌子上放了安全螺丝刀。

所以我开始工作并拆开了其中一个墨盒。

拍完他们要求的所有照片后，我接到了意想不到的电话。 我发现的不仅仅是一盒原始的《超级马里奥兄弟/猎鸭》卡带。 这是一个未记录的、以前从未见过的变体。

背面标签与之前记录的任何内容都不同。 它不是标准的纯英文文本，而是多种语言。 卡带和说明书上的制造代码也不同，表明这些游戏是 1993 年末生产的。 甚至该手册也包含以前未记录的文本。 已知的手册包括“维护或维修”一词，而这个新发现的版本则改为“维护或维修”。

特别感谢 Joseph Leo 帮助识别和记录这些墨盒和手册中发现的差异。

已知手册中的“或维修”与我们手册中的“或服务”。

也许最令人费解的是，卡带和手册上的制造日期都晚于这些游戏可能所属的每个已知的《超级马里奥兄弟》/《猎鸭子》捆绑包。

日期代码 9340 翻译为 1993 年第 40 周，对应于 8 月下旬。

我们发现的是最后一次生产运行，以及《超级马里奥兄弟/猎鸭子》的一个未被发现的变体。 可以说是任天堂历史上最受欢迎、记录最多的游戏之一。

不仅如此，几乎每个墨盒都是原始的。

但这提出了一个更大的问题：为什么要创建这些？ 为什么任天堂要在 1993 年底为不再销售的游戏机捆绑包制作新的游戏包？

我们最好的理论是，这些墨盒要么作为保修维修和翻新系统的替换库存生产，要么作为计划但从未发布的捆绑包生产。 但事实是，没有人确切知道。 目前，制造这些墨盒的确切原因只是围绕这一令人难以置信的发现的另一个谜团。

计划

与 Kevin 反复讨论后，我们决定将游戏发送给其中一家分级公司：PSA。 他们想要检查它们，验证它们的真伪，并找出这些东西到底是什么。

在与他们的一位主管进行了简短的交谈后，我决定不再将这些 97 墨盒邮寄给他们，而是在第二天亲手交付。

于是，我把所有 97 盒子弹装进随身行李，登上了凌晨 5 点的航班。 从威斯康星州密尔沃基飞往加利福尼亚州奥兰治县的航班。 没有多少事情比包里装着 97 个小电路板穿过 TSA 检查站更能让一个成年人出汗了。 我确信我会被拉到一边接受审问，但显然他们看到了更奇怪的事情。 令我惊讶的是，我没有多看一眼就通过了安检。

只是一个随身携带 97 款 NES 游戏的普通人。

抵达加州后，有人到机场接我，并带我前往PSA 总部。 我过去曾对 PSA 的很多东西进行过评分，所以看到他们的校园有多大是很有趣的。

当我到达时，我打开了游戏的包装，并在离开前与其中一位总监进行了简短的交谈。 从他们所看到的来看，毫无疑问这些游戏是真实的。 当然，分级过程会 100% 确认这一点，但从表面上看，这看起来像是真的。

我还被告知，这些游戏的状况非常好，是他们见过的最好的。

所以我把它们留在那里。 我被告知这个过程可能需要几周的时间，一旦他们知道他们正在做什么，他们就会立即通知我。

就这样，我的墨盒不见了，我就回家了。

PSA 的好处之一是，您可以直接在其网站上查看您的评分状态（至少对于视频游戏而言）。

所以在接下来的几天里，我强迫性地刷新了页面，看看其中是否有任何一个已经被评级，以及是否有可能至少其中一个将获得世界上第一个用于 NES 卡带的 PSA 10。

幸运的是，我不用等太久。 大约一周后，第一批成绩开始出现。

就在那里。

总共 12 款游戏获得了评分，其中一半多一点的游戏获得了令人难以置信的 9.8 分，有几款游戏的评分几乎达到了令人印象深刻的 9.6 分，还有一款获得了令人垂涎的、在 NES 卡带上从未见过的 PSA 10。

世界首创。
